newsitem.title: USA: Cusiana sales upset mellow foreign crude scene.
newsitem.headline: Cusiana sales upset mellow foreign crude scene.

text.p: Word that British Petroleum and Ecopetrol each sold cargoes of Colombian Cusiana crude oil upset an otherwise mellow day in the foreign crude scene, traders said.

But the Brent scene breathed a bit of life later Monday as a Wall Street player was heard buying a Brent cargo for mid-June loading at an $0.86 discount to July WTI, after the light activity in the early going.
"It was relatively a quiet day until I heard about this BP thing," said one trader.

BP was said to have sold a cargo of the light sweet Colombian Cusiana crude oil Monday for June 21-22 loading to a midcontinent U.S. independent at a $1.22 or $1.23 a barrel discount to benchmark July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing on an fob basis, trading sources said.

Colombia's state-owned Ecopetrol meanwhile was said to have closed its tender late last week on a Cusiana cargo for late June loading to a major East Coast independent refiner in a range of $1.20 to $1.23 a barrel discount to July WTI/Cushing.

The placement of the BP and Ecopetrol cargoes takes care of half the June Cusiana loading program, leaving outastanding one more Ecopetrol cargo for June 14-18 loading and one Total cargo for end June-early July loading.
In other Colombian action, rumblings were heard that a party may have snatched up the Ecopetrol tender for Vasconia crude loading around June 23-30. But that could not be confirmed.
Elsewhere in Latin America, state-owned Petroecuador is planning to offer contracts for 36,000 barrels per day of Oriente crude within the next seven days.

The Oriente tender will go to the bidder with the highest premium to a formula which currently values the crude at a $5.60 per barrel discount to WTI on the U.S. Gulf Coast and a $2.56 per barrel discount to WTI on the U.S. West Coast.

In the Brent scene, traders said the Wall Street player that reportedly picked up the mid-June cargo from another trading house could only be thinking about taking that cargo to NYMEX delivery. Neither the deal nor the intentions could be immediately confirmed.
The West African scene was mostly quiet, with an end June Qua Iboe assessment heard at a $1.96 a barrel premium to Dated Brent, traders said.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
